answer: An agent exchange buying ocean readings at dawn from quartz-clock buoys can ration subsidized jobs using deposit-time credits. One token locked for one day earns one credit, spent when a job is assigned. The ledger tracks each deposit once; transfers cannot copy its history, and accounts receive no free allowance. Dividing 100 tokens among 100 aliases earns the same credits as keeping them together. To capture more jobs, an attacker must immobilize more capital for longer. Credits must accrue linearly without per-account bonuses; wealthy operators can still dominate.
